concepts.title: International Business: Meaning and Its Reasons

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'International Business: Meaning and Its Reasons' refers to.
questions.a: International business means production and trade transactions across national boundaries, embracing import and export of goods and services, foreign direct investment, and contract manufacturing, driven by unequal distribution of resources, lower costs abroad and division of labour and specialisation among nations.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'International Business: Meaning and Its Reasons'.
questions.a: No country produces all it needs, so nations specialise where they hold advantages and trade for the rest, expanding markets beyond domestic boundaries.

questions.q: Under which section is 'International Business: Meaning and Its Reasons' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: International business (source: kebs111.txt meaning and reasons sections)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Export Import Procedure and Documentation' refers to.
questions.a: Export trade follows pre-shipment stages of enquiry, receipt of order, appointing agents, securing finance, obtaining export licence, pre-shipment finance and production, then shipment stages of customs clearance, mate's receipt, bill of lading and insurance, and post-shipment stages of invoicing, export documents, bills of exchange and realisation of proceeds.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Export Import Procedure and Documentation'.
questions.a: Key documents include proforma invoice, bill of lading, certificate of origin, letter of credit, bill of exchange and shipping bill for customs.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Export Import Procedure and Documentation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Export import procedure (source: kebs111.txt export import procedure sections)

concepts.title: WTO and the Framework of World Trade

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'WTO and the Framework of World Trade' refers to.
questions.a: The World Trade Organisation established in 1995 as successor to GATT provides the institutional framework for world trade rules, promoting free and fair trade, reducing tariffs, and settling disputes among member nations covering goods, services and intellectual property.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'WTO and the Framework of World Trade'.
questions.a: India is a founding member of the WTO, and the organisation's agreements aim at progressive liberalisation of trade for all members.
